title: I Talk Like a River
author: Jordan Scott

hero.name: Boy with stutter (narrator)
hero.description: Young boy protagonist who stutters and finds comfort by the river; appears on cover looking at water
hero.source_note: Named/distinctive cover character — source from Creative Fabrica or TPT clip art matching Sydney Smith's illustration style

ambiguous.issue: Could mean a broken object (physical) or feeling broken/sad (emotional/metaphorical)
ambiguous.reason: In this book 'broken' refers to the boy's feelings about his stutter — an emotional state; a cracked/broken heart icon conveys the metaphorical meaning better than a broken toy

ambiguous.issue: Could mean physical touch/texture or emotional feeling
ambiguous.reason: Book centres on emotional experience of stuttering; emotional 'feel' is the correct meaning

notes: This book deals with stuttering and finding one's voice through the metaphor of a river. Key vocabulary should support discussion of speech, feelings, and the natural imagery Sydney Smith uses throughout. 'stutter' may not exist in all Boardmaker libraries — an alternative search of 'speech' or a custom image may be needed. 'breathe' is central to both the river metaphor and practical speech therapy strategies depicted in the book. 'broken' and 'feel' are flagged as ambiguous due to their metaphorical use. Several words (river, morning, dad) already exist in activity_images and can be reused directly.
